key_concepts: Solid matter has definite shape, size, volume, and texture with compact molecules.
Solid materials can be changed by cutting, tearing, folding, twisting, bending, stretching
Cutting uses tools to separate materials into portions.
Tearing breaks a material by force without a cutting tool.
Folding bends an object into another shape.
Twisting forms something by holding both ends and turning them.
Crumpling presses or crushes material into irregular folds or a compact mass.
Pounding crushes material into very fine smaller pieces using force and tools.
Stretching pulls an object to make it longer or wider.
Bending forces a material from straight to curved or angular form.
Bending changes the size and shape of solid materials but does not form a new material.
Flexibility is the ability of a material to bend without breaking.
